rows.note: This is the everyday Hong Kong Cantonese term for the exhaust pipe itself.

example.english: The car's exhaust pipe is broken, and a foul smell is drifting into the garage.
example.traditional: 架車條死氣喉爛咗，成陣臭味飄入車房。
example.jyutping: gaa3 ce1 tiu4 sei2 hei3 hau4 laan6 zo2 sing4 zan6 cau3 mei6 piu1 jap6 ce1 fong4

rows.note: Use this when referring to the vehicle's exhaust system as a whole rather than just the pipe.

example.english: This car's exhaust system needs to be replaced as a whole; replacing just the pipe won't do.
example.traditional: 呢部車嘅排氣系統要成套換過，淨係換條喉唔得。
example.jyutping: ni1 bou6 ce1 ge3 paai4 hei3 hai6 tung2 jiu3 sing4 tou3 wun6 gwo3 zing6 hai6 wun6 tiu4 hau4 m4 dak1

rows.note: Use this as the everyday construction for causing someone to become completely tired; it is not used for using up a supply.

example.english: That hiking trail will exhaust me.
example.traditional: 行山嗰段路會搞到我攰晒。
example.jyutping: haang4 saan1 go2 dyun6 lou6 wui5 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 gui6 saai3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when a supply or resource has been used up completely.

example.english: During typhoons, we quickly exhaust our emergency water supply.
example.traditional: 打風嗰幾日，我哋好快就用晒啲應急食水。
example.jyutping: daa2 fung1 go2 gei2 jat6 ngo5 dei6 hou2 faai3 zau6 jung6 saai3 di1 jing3 gap1 sik6 seoi2
